Schematic diagram demonstrating menaquinone-7 (MK-7) restores mitochondrial function and determines the fate of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) via mitophagy pathways. Upon the binding of MK-7 to its nuclear receptor pregnane X receptor (PXR), the extracellular signal-regulated kinases 1/2 (ERK1/2)/cyclic AMP-responsive element-binding protein (CREB) pathway is activated, leading to an elevation expression in cellular communication network factor 2 (Ccn2). Subsequently, the Ccn2 drives PTEN- induced kinase 1 (PINK1)-dependent mitophagy, which eliminates mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and mitigates mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS). Thereby, cellular senescence is reversed and osteogenic differentiation in primary BMSCs of aged bones is enhanced. The schematic diagram was created by BioRender.com. Data shown are the mean ± SEM, with each dot indicating a single cornea analyzed from each mouse. Overall significant pattern of the correction of gene transcription back to WT levels (A–D) Endogenous transcript levels in corneas after vehicle or FLAG/PAX6 injection in WT or Sey/+ eyes were quantified with RT-ddPCR for (A) Notch1, (B) Hes1, (C) Wnt5a, and (D) Mtor. (A) In vehicle-injected WT or Sey/+ eyes, Notch1 endogenous transcripts were significantly elevated in Sey/+ eyes. After FLAG/PAX6 injection in Sey/+ eyes, the transcript levels were significantly reduced back to a level not significantly different from that in the vehicle-injected WT eyes. After FLAG/PAX6 injection in Sey/+ eyes, the transcript levels were reduced significantly for Hes1 and Mtor, back to a level not significantly different from that of vehicle-injected WT eyes. Overall, (1) there was a significant increase in the endogenous levels of these genes between vehicle-injected WT and vehicle-injected Sey/+ eyes; (2) there was a significant decrease in the endogenous levels of these genes between vehicle-injected Sey/+ and FLAG/PAX6- injected Sey/+ eyes; and (3) there was no significant difference in the endogenous levels of these genes between vehicle-injected WT and FLAG/PAX6-injected Sey/+ eyes. p ≤0.05 was considered as statistically significant. *, p ≤0.05; n, number of corneas; ns, not significant; RT-ddPCR, reverse transcription droplet digital PCR. www.moleculartherapy.org Molecular Therapy: Advances Vol. 34 September 2026 9
